title: Technology Sector Update for 05/17/2018: VSAT,HON,INTC,TTWO,NTES
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT -0.86%
AAPL -0.66%
IBM -0.12%
CSCO -3.52%
GOOG -0.39%
Technology stocks have turned solidly lower this afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 dropping almost 0.5% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a nearly 0.4% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ ViaSat ( VSAT ) was hanging on to a small gain Thursday afternoon, with shares of the broadband and communications equipment manufacturer trading in a range about 1% either side of Wednesday's closing price, after the company expanded its partnership with Honeywell ( HON ) to also include access to Viasat's high-speed Ka-band internet services to passengers flying on large- and mid-sized business jets. The equipment will be offered as part of Honeywell's GoDirect cabin connectivity suite and also includes Viasat's Global Aero 5510 terminals.
In other sector news:
+ Intel Corp. ( INTC ) was trading higher Thursday afternoon, climbing as much as 1.5%, following reports the hardware company's Mobileye unit has received a contract from an unnamed European automaker to provide 8 million vehicles with advanced driver assistance systems. The deal starts in 2021, with the Mobileye system available on selected models and certain models being fitted with a more advanced system of conditional automation, according to Reuters, citing an unidentified company official. Financial terms and other details of the contract were not disclosed.
+ Take-Two Interactive Software ( TTWO ) was rising Thursday after analysts at Benchmark Capital today raised their price target for the electronic games publisher by $5 to $135 a share and also reiterating their Buy rating for the company's stock. The move follows Take-Two Wednesday reporting Q4 net income of $0.77 per share, missing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.19 per share. Revenue for the January-to-March quarter fell to $450.3 million from $571.5 million last year but topping the $444.6 million Street view.
- NetEase ( NTES ) slid to a 16-month low on Thursday, falling almost 10% to its lowest share price since mid-January 2017 at $240.08 a share, after late Wednesday reporting a big drop in its adjusted Q1 net income compared with year-ago levels and missing Wall Street forecasts. Excluding one-time items, the Chinese online entertainment company earned RMB10.11 per American depository share, or about $1.61 per ADS, during the three months ended March 31, down sharply from last year's non-GAAP earnings of RMB32.67 per ADS and trailing the Capital IQ consensus expecting $2.23 per ADS. Revenue rose to RMB14.17 billion, or about $2.26 billion, from RMB13.64 billion during the same quarter last year and edging out the $2.22 billion Street view.
